newsitem.title: POLAND: Clinton likely to visit Poland after NATO summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton likely to visit Poland after NATO summit.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton might visit Poland after July's NATO summit in Madrid, where the pact is to invite some former communist countries to join, the Polish president's spokesman said on Monday.
"President Bill Clinton's visit to Poland after the Madrid summit is under consideration," Antoni Styrczula told a news briefing.

A source close to the Polish president said the visit was likely to start on July 10 and last one or two days, during which Clinton would address the Polish nation and hold a joint news conference with President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
The source said Clinton would then fly to Romania.

Clinton said this month Washington wanted the Madrid summit of July 8-9 to agree on inviting only Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to enter NATO initially. But he said the Western defence pact's eastward expansion would later continue, despite strong opposition by Russia.
Kwasniewski's top foreign policy aide Marek Siwiec said Clinton's visit, if it took place, " would be a signal for Poland that we are treated very seriously", private Radio Zet reported.
Siwiec added he thought such a visit was "highly probable" and that a special U.S. team had arrived in Warsaw to check the places the president would visit.
